seeds.scene: A fruit bowl with 6 bananas at varying stages of ripeness, photographed under uniform lighting. Banana A: fully green with no yellow. Banana B: green-yellow gradient, mostly green. Banana C: uniformly bright yellow with no spots. Banana D: yellow with 4-5 small brown spots. Banana E: yellow with extensive brown speckling, ~40% brown. Banana F: mostly brown-black with shrinkage. A handwritten note says 'Use most-ripe-but-not-rotten for the smoothie.'
seeds.question: Which banana should be used for the smoothie?
seeds.lever: Order banana ripeness (A<B<C<D<E<F); apply rule 'most ripe but not rotten' → exclude F (rotten), pick E.

seeds.scene: A shelf with 6 toy cars under directional lighting from the upper-left. Three cars have a true metallic finish (specular hot-spot reflections that move with viewing angle); three have a painted-silver finish (diffuse uniform appearance, no hot-spot). A close-up inset shows: car 1 has a sharp specular highlight on the hood. Car 2 has uniform pale silver shading. Car 3 has a clear hot-spot. Car 4 has uniform shading. Car 5 has a sharp specular highlight. Car 6 has uniform shading.
seeds.question: Which cars (numbers) are TRUE METALLIC, not just painted to look silver?
seeds.lever: Identify metallic via specular highlight pattern; reject diffuse silver paint.

seeds.scene: A backyard laundry line with 7 garments hanging. Visual cues for wetness: drooping (heavier when wet), darker fabric color, water droplets at hem, stretched/elongated silhouette. Visible: shirt 1 (drooping, dripping, dark fabric), shirt 2 (crisp shape, no drips), shirt 3 (slight droop, hem darker than body), pants 1 (heavy droop, water at cuff), pants 2 (no drips, even color), towel 1 (drooping, ~2x normal weight estimate), towel 2 (light, fluffy, no signs).
seeds.question: How many garments are still WET?
seeds.lever: Count items with droop + dark fabric + drips: shirt 1, shirt 3, pants 1, towel 1 = 4.

seeds.scene: Six clear glass jars on a kitchen counter, each containing white substance. Visual cues distinguish powder vs liquid: powder shows angular surface, granular texture, dust on jar walls; liquid shows flat horizontal surface and meniscus at jar walls. Jar 1: clearly granular, peaked surface. Jar 2: flat surface with meniscus. Jar 3: angled surface, dust on walls. Jar 4: flat with meniscus, very slight bubbles. Jar 5: flat, meniscus. Jar 6: granular, peaked.
seeds.question: How many jars contain a LIQUID?
seeds.lever: Distinguish powder vs liquid via surface and meniscus cues; jars 2, 4, 5 = liquid.

seeds.scene: A coffee shop counter with 5 ceramic mugs of brown beverage. Mug A: visible rising steam, no condensation. Mug B: no steam, no condensation. Mug C: heavy condensation on the outside. Mug D: ice cubes visible at the surface, condensation outside. Mug E: faint steam wisps, no outer condensation. A sign behind says 'Hot ≥ 60°C, Iced ≤ 5°C, Room ~ 22°C'.
seeds.question: Order the 5 mugs from HOTTEST to COLDEST.
seeds.lever: Steam = hot; condensation outside = cold contents; ice = coldest. Combine signals to derive ranking.

seeds.scene: A paint color sample card with 12 swatches of green: from yellow-green at left through pure green to blue-green at right, in 12 evenly-spaced steps. Each swatch is labelled with a code G01-G12. A customer's wall sample has been scotch-taped beside the card, sitting between G07 and G08 in tone — slightly closer to G07.
seeds.question: Which swatch code best matches the customer's wall sample?
seeds.lever: Fine-grained hue interpolation within a continuous spectrum; pick the closer of two adjacent samples.

seeds.scene: Five steel garden tools laid out on a tarp. Tool 1: shiny, no rust. Tool 2: surface oxidation, light orange tint. Tool 3: clear rust patches covering ~30% of surface. Tool 4: deep pitting rust, ~70% surface affected, edge looks weakened. Tool 5: red-brown solid rust covering whole surface, several holes punched through metal. A note: 'replace tools that are no longer structurally sound.'
seeds.question: Which tools should be REPLACED (structurally compromised)?
seeds.lever: Distinguish surface oxidation from structural compromise; only Tool 4 (pitting + weakened edge) and Tool 5 (holes) qualify.

seeds.scene: A fish market display with 6 whole fish on ice. Fish freshness markers: eye clarity (clear vs cloudy), gill color (red vs brown), skin sheen (glossy vs dull). Fish A: clear eyes, red gills, glossy skin. Fish B: cloudy eyes, brown gills, dull. Fish C: clear eyes, red gills, slight dullness on skin. Fish D: cloudy eyes, red gills, glossy. Fish E: very cloudy sunken eyes, brown gills, dry skin. Fish F: clear bright eyes, very red gills, glossy.
seeds.question: Order the fish from FRESHEST to OLDEST.
seeds.answer: F, A, C, D, B, E
seeds.lever: Composite ranking across three cues with conflicts (e.g., D has good gills but bad eyes); weighted aggregation.

seeds.scene: A jewelry display with 5 transparent stones cut as round brilliants. True diamonds show pinpoint sharp white sparkle (high refractive index) and multi-color fire under bright light. Glass and CZ show rainbow flashes but lack the sharp point spark. Stone 1: bright pinpoint sparkles, distinct rainbow fire. Stone 2: only rainbow fire, no sharp pinpoints. Stone 3: dull, no sparkle. Stone 4: bright pinpoint sparkles, fire. Stone 5: faint rainbow only.
seeds.question: Which stones (numbers) are likely real diamonds?
seeds.lever: Distinguish diamond's optical signature (pinpoint sparkle + fire) from glass/CZ (only rainbow); reject dull stones.

seeds.scene: A charging station with 6 phones plugged in. Each phone displays a battery icon: phone 1 shows 23% red icon. Phone 2 shows 89% green icon with lightning bolt. Phone 3 shows 100% green icon, no bolt (charging complete, idle). Phone 4 shows 56% yellow icon with bolt. Phone 5 screen is black (powered off, but cable connected). Phone 6 shows '!' battery icon (very low, possibly malfunctioning). A note says 'Disconnect any phone that is fully charged or not actively charging.'
seeds.question: How many phones should be DISCONNECTED?
seeds.lever: Identify states: phone 3 is fully charged → disconnect; phone 5 is off and not charging actively (assume not charging) → disconnect; phone 6 may still be receiving charge. Charge: 3 and 5 = 2.

seeds.scene: A theater stage under a strong RED stage light illuminating 4 fabric swatches hung on a rack. Visible appearance under red light: swatch A appears bright red, swatch B appears dark gray, swatch C appears bright red, swatch D appears nearly black. A reference card under white-light spotlight in the corner shows the same swatches under neutral light: A=white, B=blue, C=red, D=green.
seeds.question: Under the red stage light, which two swatches LOOK identical despite being different actual colors?
seeds.answer: Swatches A (white) and C (red), both appearing bright red
seeds.lever: Reason about color appearance under monochromatic light: white reflects all (looks red under red), red reflects red (looks red), blue absorbs red (dark), green absorbs red (dark).

seeds.scene: A foraging basket with 5 mushrooms photographed alongside an open field guide. Mushrooms: M1 brown cap with white gills, no ring on stem; M2 yellow cap with yellow pores under cap (no gills), white stem; M3 small brown cap with white gills, white veil ring on stem; M4 large white cap with pink/brown gills (mature), thick stem; M5 red cap with white spots. Field guide states: 'Edible: chanterelles (yellow, pores not gills), button mushrooms (white cap, pink-then-brown gills, ring). Toxic: any with white gills + ring (Amanita), red caps with white spots (Amanita muscaria).'
seeds.question: Which mushrooms (numbers) are SAFE to eat per the field guide?
seeds.lever: Apply field-guide rules to each: M2 = chanterelle (edible), M4 = button (edible), M3 = Amanita (toxic), M5 = fly agaric (toxic), M1 = white gills no ring (uncertain → not on safe list).

seeds.scene: A grocery display with 4 avocados, each with a small finger-press indent visible from a customer's earlier touch. Avocado A: indent springs back fully (firm). Avocado B: indent springs back partially. Avocado C: indent stays slightly depressed. Avocado D: indent leaves a deep dimple, surface mushy. A sign reads 'Best for tonight: yields slightly to firm pressure but not mushy.'
seeds.question: Which avocado is best for tonight per the sign?
seeds.lever: Map indent spring-back to ripeness; choose 'yields slightly but not mushy' = partial spring (B); reject firm (A), soft (C), mushy (D).

seeds.scene: A row of 5 sealed shipping boxes with various stickers: Box 1 has 'FRAGILE' + 'THIS WAY UP' + glass-icon sticker. Box 2 has only 'HEAVY 30kg' sticker. Box 3 has 'LIQUID' + 'KEEP UPRIGHT'. Box 4 has 'PERISHABLE' + dry-ice symbol. Box 5 has 'BOOKS' label.
seeds.question: Which boxes can be safely placed UPSIDE DOWN without damage?
seeds.lever: Box 1 = fragile + this way up (no), Box 3 = liquid keep upright (no), Box 4 = perishable + dry ice (no — dry ice gas vents), Box 2 = heavy but not orientation-sensitive, Box 5 = books (orientation OK).

seeds.scene: Three handwritten letters laid out together. Letter A: yellowed paper, fountain-pen ink (slight bleed-through), elegant cursive, dated 'May 4, 1948'. Letter B: bright white paper, ballpoint blue ink, blocky printing, dated '03/15/2024'. Letter C: cream paper with slight aging, fountain-pen ink, mixed cursive, undated.
seeds.question: Approximately when was Letter C most likely written? (Same era as A, between A and B, or same era as B?)
seeds.lever: Combine paper-aging cues + ink type + handwriting style; fountain-pen + cream paper + cursive places C close to A.

seeds.scene: A fabric store displays 4 bolts of fabric. Behind each bolt, a printed pattern test card with the letters 'TEST' is placed. Through bolt 1 the letters are clearly readable. Through bolt 2 the letters are blurry but legible shapes. Through bolt 3 only general shapes are visible, no letters. Bolt 4 is fully opaque.
seeds.question: Order bolts from MOST translucent to LEAST.
seeds.lever: Translucency = how much detail passes through; rank by readable detail of background test card.

seeds.scene: A wall with a water leak shows a damp patch with concentric rings: dark wet center (~20cm radius), medium-dark ring (~30cm radius), light damp ring (~40cm radius), dry wall outside. Three thumbtacks marked T1, T2, T3 are placed at distances 15cm, 35cm, 50cm from the leak center.
seeds.question: Which thumbtack is in the medium-dark damp zone?
seeds.lever: T1 (15cm) is in dark wet center; T2 (35cm) is in medium-dark ring; T3 (50cm) is in dry zone.

seeds.scene: A photo of a white card on a table, taken under a tungsten incandescent lamp. The white card appears warm yellow-orange. Beside the card, four colored balls. The image's actual ball appearances: ball A appears orange (looks orange but might be white), ball B appears red (looks red, might actually be red or magenta), ball C appears greenish (might be green or cyan), ball D appears very pale yellow.
seeds.question: Using the white card as reference, what is ball A's TRUE color (under neutral light)?
seeds.lever: White-balance correction: the white card appears yellow-orange under tungsten, so subtract that color cast from all objects. Ball A appearing orange = white shifted by tungsten cast = actually white.

seeds.scene: Five powder samples on watch glasses on a lab bench. Sample 1: uniform pure-white fine powder. Sample 2: white powder with a few visible black specks. Sample 3: light yellow tint, uniform. Sample 4: white powder with clearly mixed-in colored crystals (red, blue). Sample 5: uniform pure-white but with lumps (caking — possibly absorbed moisture). Lab notebook: 'pure NaCl is white, fine, uniform; reject anything visibly contaminated or moisture-affected.'
seeds.question: Which samples (numbers) pass the purity test?
seeds.lever: Sample 2 has specks (contamination), 3 is yellow (impurity or wrong compound), 4 is mixed, 5 is moisture-affected; only 1 passes.

seeds.scene: Five copper sculptures in a park. Their patina ranges from new bright copper (just-installed) through brown oxidation to deep green verdigris (decades old). S1: bright copper, no patina. S2: brown-orange uniform patina. S3: brown-orange with small green spots starting. S4: mostly green with some brown showing through. S5: full deep green verdigris uniform. A plaque says 'sculptures installed in 2025, 2018, 2010, 2000, 1985 (order unknown).'
seeds.question: Which sculpture was installed in 2025?
seeds.lever: Order patina age S1<S2<S3<S4<S5; map to install dates 2025>2018>2010>2000>1985; newest = 2025 = S1.
